facility_roles.quote: The GERDA experiment searched for neutrinoless double-beta (0νββ) decay of 76Ge by operating Ge detectors made from 76Ge enriched material in a 64 m3 liquid argon cryostat located in Hall A of LNGS.

intervals.label: Phase I data taking
intervals.note: Checked against the full text of the cited status paper; the quote is the paper's own sentence.
intervals.quote: The first phase (Phase I), from November 2011 to May 2013, accumulated an exposure of 21.6 kg⋅yr with a background of about 10−2 cts/(keV⋅kg⋅yr) at Qββ

intervals.label: Phase II data taking
intervals.note: Both bounds are stated in the PRL paper (Phase II data collected December 2015 to November 2019). The official GERDA home page separately states that data taking stopped in February 2020.
intervals.quote: GERDA Phase II data were collected between December 2015 and November 2019.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.locator: Max Planck Institute for Physics, "The former GERDA experiment"
intervals.note: The collaboration's own institute page describes GERDA in the past tense ("the former GERDA experiment") and states a nine-year lifetime; no fetched source gives an exact shutdown day. LEGEND-200 assumed the Hall A infrastructure afterward.
intervals.quote: After its nine-year lifetime, the GERDA experiment was able to rule out with 90 percent certainty that the half-life of neutrinoless double beta decay was less than 1.8 x 10^26 years.

quantity.note: Reported as an exposure (mass times time, kg·yr); the kg figure is stored as the value and `display` carries the authoritative exposure. The quote is the abstract sentence of the final-results paper.
quantity.quote: When combined with the result of Phase I, no signal is observed after 127.2 kg·yr of total exposure.

quantity.note: Recorded as a lower limit, not a measured value; the unit 'yr' is used descriptively and `display` carries the authoritative figure (of order 10²⁶ years).
quantity.quote: is set at $T_{1/2}>1.8\times10^{26}$ yr at 90% C.L.

name: GERDA
notes: No INSPIRE experiment lookup was performed; external.inspire_experiment is left empty rather than guessed.
Collaboration formation date and precise Phase I/Phase II day-level dates were not found in any source consulted; see the collaboration record and interval notes above for what is and is not sourced.
GERDA is superseded by LEGEND-200, which reuses much of the Hall A infrastructure (lineage: predecessor).

The Phase I and Phase II intervals have a 30-month gap (2013-06 to 2015-11) with no recorded status; this corresponds to GERDA's known upgrade/shutdown period between phases, but no source consulted gives a sourced interval for it. It is left as an unrecorded gap rather than guessed.

physics_goals.locator: MPP institute page "The former GERDA experiment"; MPI-HD GERDA home page (76Ge 0vbb search)
physics_goals.quote: investigated whether the neutrino was its own antiparticle. Neutrinos of this type are known as “Majorana” neutrinos. ... GERDA also employed detectors made of germanium-76. The nuclei of this material can decay, at least in theory, via neutrinoless double beta decay.
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 76Ge to test whether the neutrino is its own antiparticle (a Majorana fermion)

summary.plain: A neutrino experiment buried under a mountain in Italy that searched for a rare radioactive process in germanium atoms. Finding it would prove neutrinos are their own antiparticles. GERDA ran from 2011 to 2019 and found no signal, only setting a limit.
summary.technical: GERmanium Detector Array (GERDA): search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 76Ge using bare enriched-germanium detectors operated in a 64 m³ liquid-argon cryostat in Hall A of LNGS. Phase I (2011-2013) and Phase II (2015-2019) accumulated 127.2 kg·yr of exposure and set T1/2 > 1.8×10²⁶ yr (90% C.L.); superseded by LEGEND-200.

unique_capabilities.quote: met the design goal to collect an exposure of 100 kg·yr in a background-free regime
unique_capabilities.value: Bare (naked) enriched-germanium detectors submerged directly in liquid argon, which serves as both cooling medium and active shield, achieving a background-free regime
